certified_entry_comparisons.title: Strict native Markdown and JSON agent definitions with source identity
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
The native parser treats the frontmatter name as identity, independent of the filename, and validates a strict schema before creating a frozen definition. It retains the source hash and source attribution so discovery, model listing and later child acceptance can detect which definition was selected.

Frontmatter parsing normalizes CRLF and lone CR to LF; it recognizes an opening prefix '---' only at byte/string start and the first '\n---' delimiter after offset3, parses the intervening YAML and trims the extracted body. No delimiter or no frontmatter.name means not-agent. A YAML parse failure is invalid even without a usable name. Native fields are checked with TypeBox; unknown keys produce exact diagnostics, with replacement suggestions for fallbackModel/fallback_model, thinkingLevel, top_p/top-p, mcpTools/mcp_tools, adapters, startupTimeoutMs/startup-timeout-ms and iceUnsafeHostExec/ice-unsafe-host-exec. The startupTimeoutMs suggestion still names legacy ice.subagents.defaults.startupTimeoutMs; do not treat that suggestion as an active V2 setting. Empty trimmed Markdown body is invalid. Issues retain a name only when it matches the agent-name pattern. Diagnostics deduplicate; ordinary schema errors stop once the result reaches16, but the additionalProperties branch can append multiple messages before that check.

JSON input undefined is empty; null/nonobject/array produces an expected-object-map issue. Each own map entry supplies its identity and is validated independently, retaining valid neighbors. A JSON entry may not repeat name; description and prompt are required. JSON prompt is passed through without a trim/nonblank check beyond the schema's minLength. Definition construction strips name/description/prompt from fields, normalizes a tools comma string by split/trim/drop-empty, redacts the prompt using the shared credential-pattern redactor, shallow-freezes the definition/fields/diagnostics, and preserves limited=false. Markdown sourceHash is SHA-256 of the original input content; JSON sourceHash is SHA-256 of canonical field JSON. Canonical JSON sorts object keys, omits undefined object properties, preserves array order and otherwise uses JSON.stringify. It is not a signature or authority grant.

Agent names match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$. Description maxLength1024; tools may be a list or comma string(maxLength4096); selected lists have at most64 entries of1..256 characters; model is one1..256-character string or1..8 such strings. initialPrompt maxLength4096; tags at most8 of1..32 characters; temperature0..2 and topP0..1. Permission rules and presentation colors use shared vocabularies. The declared maxPromptBytes=65536 is a TypeBox maxLength for JSON prompt, not an explicit UTF-8 byte check in this parser. Markdown body has no separate64KiB parser check; discovery separately caps the entire file at128KiB. Later preflight/context limits must be audited separately rather than inferred from these names.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: Native Markdown requires {name,description} plus a nonempty body. JSON map entries require {description,prompt}. Optional fields: tools,disallowedTools,model,thinking,permissionMode,permissions:{allow?,ask?,deny?},background,isolation,contextFiles,skills,prompts,context,mcp,requiredMcpServers,hooks,initialPrompt,spawns,color,hidden,tags,temperature,topP. Reserved provenance fields: ice-agent-pack(maxLength256),ice-agent-pack-source(maxLength1024),ice-agent-pack-sha256(^[a-f0-9]{64}$). thinking=off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra; isolation=none|worktree; permissionMode=inherit|plan|review|build|bubble. ParsedAgentSource=not-agent|invalid{issue}|agent{definition}; issue availability=invalid|untrusted. Resolved definition carries name,description,prompt,fields,source,sourcePath?,sourceHash,diagnostics,limited. No provider is contacted by parsing.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Opt-in Claude agent compatibility with explicit model aliases
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Compatibility parsing maps recognized Claude fields into the native definition schema and records warnings for discarded fields. It remains a project source with project trust and lower precedence than native project agents.

Invalid YAML and absent frontmatter.name follow the native parser's invalid/not-agent behavior. Known keys are name,description,tools,disallowedTools,model,effort,permissionMode,mcpServers,hooks,skills,initialPrompt,memory,background,isolation,color; unknown keys produce warnings rather than native-schema unknown-key failure. Tool lists accept comma strings; exact case-sensitive mappings are Read→read,Grep→grep,Glob→find,LS→ls,Bash→bash,Edit→edit,MultiEdit→edit,Write→write, with unknown names preserved for later resolution.

For string model, trim first: case-insensitive inherit becomes inherit; otherwise use an exact global compat.modelAliases key, then accept a reference containing '/', else warn and set limited=true. A nonstring model is not copied. effort is copied to thinking only for an exact supported thinking value. permissionMode copies only plan or bubble; default is silently omitted and other supplied values warn and are discarded. background and initialPrompt copy through; skills normalize as a tool-style comma list; only worktree isolation is copied, with other values warned. Colors map red→error,green→success,yellow/orange→warning,blue/purple/pink/cyan→accent; other colors are dropped. mcpServers,hooks,memory always warn and are not copied. Native schema validation and nonempty trimmed body still apply. Source hash uses original content, prompt is redacted, source is project-compat and warning diagnostics remain with the accepted definition. limited definitions are excluded from callable listing.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: Global opt-in consumer: ice.subagents.compat.claudeAgents (default false) and compat.modelAliases (string map), resolved by V2 settings. Source path pattern .claude/agents/**/*.md. parseClaudeCompatAgentMarkdown(content,sourcePath,modelAliases)->ParsedAgentSource. No implicit model alias service, permission upgrade, MCP connection or legacy delegate tool is installed.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Bounded agent discovery, trust filtering and whole-definition precedence
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Discovery walks bounded directories and deduplicates physical Markdown files before applying name precedence. Loading preserves separate issue/shadow/disabled records and caches only under an explicit caller key, so catalog refresh and child contract reuse can be controlled separately.

The default global definition root is the sibling agents directory of the normal agent directory: ~/.ice/agents when the normal agent directory is ~/.ice/agent. An environment override or an explicit effective agentDir differing from getAgentDir uses <agentDir>/agents. The code consumes ENV_AGENT_DIR through legacy-compatible getIceEnv; environment-name resolution belongs to config/compat. Project directories are collected nearest-first from canonical cwd, with at most64 ancestor steps and no inclusion of canonical home. If no Git boundary is found, only cwd is considered. A nested repository inside the session project widens the stop boundary to the session project's root; otherwise the nearest repository root wins. Linked worktrees fall back to the standard main checkout's agent directory when the worktree root lacks its own directory, even if a nearer nested directory was found. Fallback requires common Git metadata to identify an ordinary main/.git layout.

For each existing root, recurse through at most depth8 (root depth0), sort names with localeCompare, skip dot-prefixed entries and accept case-sensitive .md regular files. Symlinks may be followed only when their canonical target stays inside the canonical root; escaping targets produce a diagnostic. A shared seen set uses device:inode when inode is truthy, otherwise canonical path, so physical files load once across roots. Count unique candidate Markdown files before size/read checks; after512 files in one root stop its remainder and report the cap. Files above128KiB are skipped. Inaccessible directory/stat entries are silently skipped; read failure on an otherwise accepted file is diagnostic. A file enters seen before count/size/read checks. Directory symlink recursion has the depth bound but no separate visited-directory set.

Actual collection order is managed files first, then native project, opt-in project-compat, user, package, user-settings JSON, project-settings JSON and flag JSON; managed-first protects inode dedup. Untrusted project files are still discovered/parsed but yield only an untrusted name/path/diagnostic and never an active definition/prompt. Untrusted project JSON contributes untrusted records for valid parsed definitions and omits its parser issues. Precedence by name is builtin<package<user<user-settings<project-compat<project<project-settings<flag<managed. Within the same source, first input wins; nearer project roots therefore win. Replacement is whole-definition, never field merge. Every previous winner becomes a shadow record. Winners sort by localeCompare name; disabled names are removed unless the winning source is managed. AgentDefinitionCache holds one key/value and refreshes only when key changes or invalidate is called; it does not itself install watchers.

Sources/paths: ~/.ice/agents,custom <agentDir>/agents,.ice/agents,.claude/agents,packageAgentDirs,explicit managedAgentsDir; settings ice.subagents.agents and disabledAgents; startup --agents. No managed directory is searched unless supplied. All paths here were read as source strings only; actual user configuration was not accessed.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Built-in agents and incremental model-visible catalog
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Built-ins are ordinary lowest-precedence definitions with stable source hashes and no child-spawn names. The listing helper filters unavailable definitions, computes changes by name/source hash and emits a compact custom-message description for the caller to insert into model context.

Built-in names in order are general,explore,plan,review,worker. general requests inherited child-safe tools. explore and plan explicitly request read,grep,find,ls, set permissionMode=plan and contextFiles=false. review uses the same four tools with permissionMode=review. worker uses permissionMode=build and isolation=worktree. All set spawns=[]; prompts require bounded-scope work and concrete evidence/reporting, but actual authority comes from runtime guards. Each returned record/fields/diagnostics is frozen; source=builtin and sourceHash hashes canonical builtin content.

callableAgentDefinitions removes hidden and limited definitions. Every requiredMcpServers entry must be a case-insensitive substring of at least one available server name; this helper does not use glob matching or connect a server. Tool summary displays requested list items minus exact disallowed string matches; for omitted or ['*'] lists it says All tools or All tools except. That description is not the effective runtime permission set.

Listing state is Map<name,sourceHash>. With no previous state, emit full=true and every callable record as added; otherwise report newly added, same-name/different-hash changed and missing-name removed. next records every current callable name. Unchanged nonfull delta returns undefined. Full empty text explicitly says no agents are available. Message includes header, agent lines, optional removed names and an agent_control action=agents footer. Default target is8192 UTF-8 bytes: first try full descriptions/tool summaries, then descriptions sliced to80 JS code units, then one names-only line. The final names-only fallback and removed line are returned without a final byte check, so the helper does not guarantee the advertised cap for arbitrarily large catalogs/removal sets; the inspected60-agent test proves only its fixture. Callers own listing-state reset and delivery around compaction/navigation/model changes.

The custom message is the catalog interface; no additional listing model tool is declared by this module.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Strict scoped V2 settings and monotonic numeric limits
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
The V2 resolver validates global and trusted-project scopes independently, then composes a typed result with diagnostics and deprecation notices. Storage is separate: this entry owns accepted keys, defaults and exact merge semantics.

The accepted keys are enabled,v2,defaultAgent,maxDepth,maxConcurrent,askTimeoutMs,foregroundDetachMs,bashTimeoutMs,turnTimeoutMs,idleTimeoutMs,idleAlertMs,permissions,agents,disabledAgents,compat. Undefined/null is an empty scope. Nonrecord/array is invalid. Undefined-valued keys are skipped. Unknown keys diagnose; deprecated defaults,allowedRoles,roleDefaults,restrictions,modelSelection,concurrency,routeTiers are ignored with deprecation records. Any validation errors empty that entire scope, not merely the bad field; launch code must separately refuse diagnostics. An untrusted project is not parsed at all. v2 accepts boolean but does not select an alternate implementation.

enabled defaults true and requires neither scope false. defaultAgent takes project,global,then general. maxDepth defaults0,integer0..4 and is reserved by runtime; maxConcurrent defaults4,integer>=1 with no upper schema bound. Depth,concurrency,Bash,turn and idle ceilings use min(global value or bundled default,project value or Infinity). askTimeoutMs is global-only,default600000,min1000,max3600000. foregroundDetachMs defaults60000,range0..3600000; idleAlertMs defaults300000,range0..86400000. Their shorten-only merge ignores a project0, lets a positive project enable a globally-disabled0 timer, otherwise takes the shorter. Therefore current idleAlertMs does accept a trusted-project shortening despite older global-only documentation. Bash timeout default600000,turn1800000,idle600000; each1000..86400000. Permissions retain user/settings and project/settings origins, agents remain separate maps for source precedence, disabled names union, and compat is global-only.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Permission rule grammar, tool subjects and conservative shell decomposition
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
The evaluator combines all matching rules using deny before ask before allow, then applies opaque-command and mode ceilings. A tool invocation is only as permissive as its most restrictive subject. Shell processing is a bounded textual approximation rather than a shell parser.

A rule is a tool glob, optionally followed by a1..512-character parenthesized subject glob; tool syntax is '*' or an alphabetic first character followed by at most127 alphanumeric,underscore,dot,asterisk orhyphen characters. parsePermissionRule does not trim. Path glob '*' stays inside one component, '**' crosses components and '**/' also matches no prefix; '?' is one nonseparator character. Nonpath '*' matches any characters across newlines, while '?' uses regex dot. Matching is anchored. Decisions carry matching origin scope(builtin,managed,user,project,cli,session) and carrier(settings,agent-definition,compat-definition,flag,grant). No matching rule uses the supplied fallback. Stable sorting preserves equal-ranked match order.

read/grep/find/ls extract a read path; edit/write extract edit-write. A nonempty string args.path resolves lexically against cwd, otherwise '.'. In-cwd subjects use relative slash paths; outside paths use absolute values and add an external_directory subject. Unknown or unclassified adapters are mutation-adapter, never read. agent tasks contribute delegation subjects using the requested agent names. Bash splits on &&,||,semicolon,newline,unpaired '&' and '|', excluding descriptor operators by the literal regex; it does not honor shell quotes. Any command/process substitution syntax ($(...),backticks,<(,>()) marks every command fragment opaque. File output redirection marks that fragment opaque after allowing descriptor duplication and recognized /dev/null redirection; this cannot serve as complete shell-language validation.

Opaque Bash is capped at ask unless explicit subYolo is active; explicit denies and asks still win. Plan/review allow read, cap external-directory/delegation at ask and hard-deny Bash, edit-write and mutation-adapter. This is stricter than stale reference prose claiming Bash approval in those modes. Session Bash grant prefixes split whitespace, discard tokens beginning '-', then retain a known command/subcommand arity(git/npm/pnpm/yarn/bun/cargo/docker/kubectl/go/uv/pip2,gh3; package-manager run3), otherwise one token; they are not parsed command ASTs.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: PermissionDecision=deny|ask|allow. PermissionSubject={tool,value?,pathMode,subjectClass,opaque?}; classes read|edit-write|bash|mutation-adapter|external-directory|delegation. AgentPermissionMode=inherit|plan|review|build|bubble. APIs globMatches,parsePermissionRule,extractPermissionSubjects,evaluatePermission,evaluatePermissionSubjects,bashGrantPrefix. Evaluation returns decision,matched rules/origins and limitedByMode. Errors from invalid schema belong to SUB-005/SUB-001, not the matcher.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Child permission ceilings and source-sensitive authority raisers
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Derivation starts from the class-specific child ceiling, applies an eligible raiser, narrows by child rules and agent mode, and finally intersects the parent decision. The final parent intersection is unconditional; sub-yolo, worktrees and allow rules cannot defeat it.

Read and delegation inherit the parent ceiling. edit-write and Bash start at ask; edit-write can rise through sub-yolo,user allow,managed allow or worktree isolation, while Bash can rise through sub-yolo,user allow ormanaged allow. Mutation adapters can rise only through user ormanaged allow, not sub-yolo orworktrees. External directories are capped at ask unless sub-yolo ormanaged allow raises them; user allow does not suffice. An opaque shell subject cannot use a rule-based raiser without subYolo. All child rules still narrow the result, and plan/review hard limits apply afterward. raisedBy is returned only when the result is actually allow.

Raiser detection checks origin.scope=user ormanaged, not the carrier. Project rules therefore cannot lift a ceiling; a claim that every agent-definition carrier is categorically excluded would exceed this helper's implementation. The runtime must assign definition origins correctly and revalidate current authority at execution. The pure childDelegationTools helper offers agent andagent_control only when depth<maxDepth,spawns is nonempty,the parent has agent and the target decision is not deny; it never offers agent_patch. This helper does not prove recursive V2 delegation is currently wired.

The parentDecision argument is caller-supplied. In the active V2 guard, external_directory receives a special parent branch: plan denies; an authorized sub-yolo host allows; otherwise it asks. That branch precedes ordinary parent rule-set evaluation (SUB-019), so the first-pass statement that sub-yolo can never permit external directories is not the current implementation.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: Child derivation context: childRuleSets,agentMode,subYolo,worktree. Output {decision,raisedBy?}, where raisedBy=sub-yolo|user-allow|managed-allow|worktree-isolation. CHILD_MUTATION_CEILING is the authoritative raiser table. Delegation helper output={tools,spawnable}; denial is per target and ask remains eligible for later approval. No persisted grant or new RPC operation occurs in this pure step.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Approval broker with foreground prompts, inbox routing and owner cancellation
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
The broker owns pending approval identity and settlement, while callers own the policy decision and applying an offered session rule. Automated checks precede user interaction; absent an appropriate channel, the answer is deny.

Pre-aborted requests and disposed brokers deny immediately. automatedCheck is raced with the external abort signal and may return allow,deny orask; an ordinary checker exception propagates. There is no broker timeout around that preliminary automated check, only external cancellation. Afterward foreground requests use interactive when available; other requests require hasInbox. No channel denies with source no-channel. Duplicate pending IDs throw. A pending waiter records queuedAt/deadline, default600000ms timeout and its own AbortController. It is inserted before adding the external abort listener and rechecks aborted state to close that race. onChange observes the current pending array.

Interactive promise rejection becomes a user denial. respond returns false for an unknown/settled ID. deny settles deny; allow-once and allow-session settle allow, with the latter returning only the sessionRule already offered by the request. No arbitrary new rule is accepted here. Settlement deletes the waiter,cancels its timer,removes the external abort listener,aborts the UI controller,resolves and notifies. denyOwner cancels only that owner with source disposed; dispose cancels all and rejects future asks. onChange exceptions are not swallowed by this class, so a host should keep that callback nonthrowing. A broker does not itself persist grants.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: ApprovalRequest={id,ownerSessionId,childId,agent,name?,tool,summary,sessionRule?,foreground}. Responses allow-once|allow-session|deny. Resolution={decision:allow|deny,source:automated|user|timeout|aborted|disposed|no-channel,sessionRule?}. API request(request,signal?),respond(id,response),pending,denyOwner(ownerSessionId),dispose(). Dependencies include a host UI/inbox adapter; RPC method ownership belongs to the integration entry.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Startup authorization for sub-yolo and reduced delegated shell environment
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Startup argument normalization rejects ambiguous or noninteractive sub-yolo configurations before the subagent extension can use the grant. Runtime authorization then binds the grant to the current build mode,trusted project,recorded Bash grant and current active parent tools.

Normalization activates when --sub-yolo or --allow-external is present. Those flags accept bare or =true only; =false and duplicate occurrences throw. Both require a single explicit --ice-mode build; contradictory or duplicate mode flags fail. Both grant modes reject --no-approve/-na by presence. Sub-yolo additionally requires --ice-allow-bash true exactly once and requires both TTY unless explicitly in single --mode rpc. Print mode and non-RPC output modes are incompatible. --allow-external alone may be headless. Bare grant flags normalize to =true. These checks authorize nothing about project trust by themselves.

authorizeUnsafeSubagentHostExecution returns undefined unless startupSubYolo is true. An active request requires capability state,build mode,trusted project,recorded Bash allowance,Bash currently active and an interactive TUI or RPC context with hasUI. It freezes the current parent tool names and allowExternal. Delegated Bash environment separately copies only defined LANG,LC_ALL,LC_CTYPE,LC_MESSAGES,LC_MONETARY,LC_NUMERIC,LC_TIME,PATH,SHELL,TERM,TMPDIR. It does not inherit arbitrary credentials or stale session variables, but this whitelist is not an OS sandbox and the retained shell/path still influence execution.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: Startup flags --sub-yolo[=true],--allow-external[=true],--ice-allow-bash[=true],--ice-mode build; interacting flags --mode rpc,--print/-p,--no-approve/-na. Runtime grant includes parentActiveTools and allowExternal. createDelegatedShellEnvironment(source) returns a fresh ProcessEnv whitelist. The environment is passed to the child Bash adapter; host session metadata behavior is separately TOOLS-002.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Strict hook configuration, source precedence and revocable handler registration
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Hook configuration is strict data; executable handlers are registered separately under an owner object. Resolution orders mandatory global hooks,optional global hooks and trusted-project hooks, and definition/call selections can choose only known optional hooks.

Each definition accepts only id,event,roles,kind,timeoutMs,maxOutputBytes,required. ID is trimmed and matches [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,127}; roles are trimmed lowercase,deduplicated,nonempty and at most64UTF-8 bytes each, with no role-count bound. kind defaults in-process, alternatively command. timeout defaults1500ms,range1..30000; output defaults8192bytes,range1..32768; required defaults true. At most32 definitions and no duplicate IDs in a scope. Undefined/null hooks disables; enabled defaults true when definitions are nonempty. Global explicit disabled overrides project hooks. Project trust defaults true if a direct resolver caller omits it; runtime callers pass current trust.

An existing hook ID is never replaced by a lower layer's body/source. A required collision with a different event throws; a same-event required declaration can promote an optional global hook to required. Optional roleHookIds and callHookIds form a union; unknown IDs and attempts to select a mandatory hook throw. Empty selection suppresses optional hooks. Required hooks bypass the resolver's role-selection filter, but dispatcher eligibility still applies event and roles. Registration is a WeakMap keyed by the trusted owner,with duplicate ID rejection; unregister only removes the same handler reference. The integration snapshots handlers and rechecks registration identity at dispatch, so removal/replacement revokes a stale handler. The registration object, not arbitrary event data, conveys implementation authority.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: Namespace ice.hooks={enabled?,definitions?,commandPolicy?}. Events: subagent.beforeLaunch,started,beforeTool,afterTool,checkpoint,attention,beforeAccept,completed,failed,cancelled. Decision events are beforeLaunch,beforeTool,beforeAccept; remaining events are observational. Hook definitions refer to IDs,never source-code strings. API parseIceHooksSettings,resolveIceSubagentHooks,registerIceSubagentHook,getIceSubagentHookHandlers; default integration can ask the current UI but no-UI/print/json returns false. V2 current runtime does not dispatch checkpoint orattention merely because these values are accepted.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Bounded hook dispatch, durable intent and fail-closed decision events
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
The dispatcher serializes eligible hooks and keeps denial sticky: later hooks receive skipped-deny records without executing. Required decision hooks fail closed; observational failures become diagnostics rather than taking over the ordinary agent loop.

Payload sanitization redacts credential-like keys(api-key/token/secret/password/authorization/cookie),redacts text,limits depth to4 and arrays/object entries to32,handles cycles and unsupported values,then deep-freezes. Strings are first4096UTF-8 bytes plus an ellipsis,which may include a replacement character if cut mid-codepoint. A JSON payload above16384bytes is replaced by a digest-only truncated object. Fingerprint is the first16hex SHA-256 characters. Every dispatch record carries UUIDeventId,ownerSessionId,runId,attempt1|2,hookId,event,outcome,required,reason?,durationMs and observational.

onIntent is awaited before the handler and consumes the same configured deadline. Remaining handler execution and approval share that original deadline; abort/timeouts abort the hook controller,while a noncooperating underlying promise may finish later without changing the settled result. Missing required handlers fail; optional ones diagnose. Only continue|deny|ask is valid, and observers may only continue. Ask requires requestApproval; missing channel denies. Approved asks retain ask in their record while allowing overall continuation. beforeLaunch may append at most4 context items per hook,each trimmed/redacted nonempty and<=4096bytes; other events reject additions. A later denial can leave prior additions in the returned array,so the caller must discard a denied result.

Required decision exceptions,invalid output,intent failure and timeout deny. Optional decision errors and all observational errors continue with redacted diagnostics,including required observers. Append/outcome/observation sink errors are caught; intent failure is authoritative. The integration appends custom journal type ice-subagent-hook-v1 with schemaVersion1 and phase intent|outcome,flushes intents durably and treats outcomes as best effort. Runtime keeps at most64 observed records in its local projection. beforeLaunch gates before child acceptance; permission guard runs before beforeTool; beforeAccept denial converts a completed turn to failed; started/afterTool/terminal events observe execution.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: Handler input contains hook,event,ownerSessionId,runId,attempt?,role?,payload,signal?. Output {outcome:continue|deny|ask,reason?,contextAdditions?:[{content}]}. Dispatcher output {outcome,records,diagnostics,contextAdditions}; reasons are redacted and bounded. APIs dispatchSubagentHookDecision,dispatchSubagentHookObservation,flushSubagentHookObservations. Journal record identifies intent/outcome but is never instructions to replay external effects.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Host-pinned command hooks with literal argv and bounded subprocess I/O
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Command policy is host configuration rather than an agent-supplied command string. Dispatch rechecks current authority,configured identities and optional user approval before spawning literal argv without a shell.

Undefined policy disables and defaults approval ask. Strict keys are enabled,approval,commands; a present policy requires boolean enabled and a commands object with at most32 named definitions. Each command requires a files object, even when empty. A command accepts argv,cwd,sha256,files only. argv has1..32 strings,each no NUL and<=4096bytes; argv[0] andcwd must be absolute. Executable SHA-256 is64lowercasehex; files is at most16 absolute-path SHA pairs. Before spawn,canonical cwd must remain inside canonical workspace; executable and each pinned file must be regular and realpath(path)===resolve(path),rejecting symlink aliases,then content hashes must match. Hash reads have no explicit file-size bound. This is a pre-spawn identity check with a path-use race,not an atomic executable handle pin.

Execution requires enabled/id/current authorization; approval ask must return true,then abort and authority are checked again. Integration rejects enabled project command policy and uses only the global policy. Current authorization requires a non-read-only target,both current trust checks,build capability,recorded Bash grant,Bash still active and JSON equality with the accepted global policy. In-process handlers with the same ID are replaced by command handlers. Input is JSON {schemaVersion:1,event,ownerSessionId,runId,attempt,role?,payload},at most32768bytes. Spawn is shell:false,detached off Windows,windowsHide,three pipes and environment exactly LANG=C.UTF-8,LC_ALL=C.UTF-8. stdout andstderr are bounded separately by hook.maxOutputBytes; stderr text is discarded. First failure stops stdin,kills the tracked process tree,and after1000ms destroys streams/unrefs before rejecting if cleanup has not settled. Deadline,abort,stdin/spawn errors,nonzero exit,oversize and malformed JSON all fail.

Output requires schemaVersion1,outcome continue|deny|ask,optional string reason and contextAdditions,with no extra keys; additions are validated by SUB-011. Exact parser discrepancy: policy approval validation checks String(value.approval??'ask') against ask|allow but stores the original uncoerced value. A malformed host value such as ['ask'] therefore passes that check yet fails the later strict equality approval==='ask',skipping the prompt. This is a source-read conditional behavior of malformed global host configuration,not a reproduced execution. The Rust port should use strict enum deserialization and document this deliberate correction.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: ice.hooks.commandPolicy={enabled:boolean,approval?:ask|allow,commands:Record<id,{argv:string[],cwd:string,sha256:string,files:Record<absolutePath,sha256>}>}; omitting the whole policy disables it, while present policy requires enabled,commands and each files map (empty maps are valid). JSON stdin/stdout protocol version1. No PATH or other ambient environment inherited. API parseIceCommandHookPolicy,createIceCommandHookHandler. Tests source-cover environment,authority,missing approval,changed script,output flood,deadline and malformed response; they were not run.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Frozen child runtime contract and hash-checked transcript initialization
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Each child has a durable lifetime ID and a deeply frozen version2 contract. Canonical SHA-256 ties the child transcript's initialization to the parent registry; it is an integrity reference,not a signature or permission grant.

IDs are ag_ plus26lowercase base32 characters; group display handles are agg_ plus26; optional names are lowercase alphanumeric/hyphen1..40 without underscores. Generation uses17random bytes encoded to26symbols,130bits despite the128-bit comment. Construction verifies ID and depth0..maxDepth,structured-clones input,redacts system/initial prompts,adds an ISO createdAt and recursively freezes. Canonical serialization sorts object keys,omits undefined object members and preserves array order. parseChildRuntimeContract validates object/version/ID and expected hash,not a complete recursive schema; a Rust parser may deliberately add stricter shape validation.

Contract groups: owner/root/optional parent child/depth; definition source/path/sourceHash/resolvedDefinitionHash/selected hook IDs; actual redacted system and initial prompts,contextFiles flag,resource hashes and selected resource records; provider/model/thinking/temperature/topP/skipped candidates; frozen tools{name,access,adapterId?,fingerprint?},normalized rules{rule,decision,scope},roots,targets,MCP servers,spawns,maxDepth,subYolo,agentMode,parentMode,parentPolicyHash,worktree flag; result schema,acceptance andtask contract; isolation baseline/repository/worktree fields. Carrier provenance is dropped by freezeRules and reconstructed as settings on reopen; scope remains. SOURCE_SCOPE assigns package/user/user-settings→user,managed→managed,project sources→project,flag→cli,builtin→builtin,so user/package definitions can supply rule raisers under SUB-007.

Child files live at <parent-session-dir>/subagents/<validated-parent-session-id>/. SessionManager creates a normal child session using the childID and optional parent-session path,appends first custom ice-subagent-v2-init{contract,contractHash},then flushes durably before launch. Reopen finds the first matching init entry,checks its stored hash equals the registry hash and verifies the serialized contract. findInterruptedToolCalls tracks unresolved calls only from the latest assistant message,clearing on each assistant; recovery text names unknown outcomes and advises inspection,never replay.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: CHILD_RUNTIME_CONTRACT_VERSION=2. First custom type ice-subagent-v2-init. ChildRuntimeContract exact shape at source53–129. buildChildRuntimeContract,hashChildRuntimeContract,serializeChildRuntimeContract,parseChildRuntimeContract,createChildSession,openChildSession. Baseline child-resume checks owner,tombstone,live tool childSafe/access/adapter identity/fingerprint,sub-yolo continuation,build→plan mutation andmodel availability; runtime adds current trust/resource/policy checks.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Explicit child-safe adapters, MCP bridge and capability fingerprints
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Adapter registration is an explicit host assertion of independent child-safe execution,not a tool-description heuristic. The runtime intersects active parent tools with known builtins or live adapters and records the selected capability identity in the child contract.

At most32 registrations per owner; name regex [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63},adapter ID [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{0,127},origin similar with alphanumeric first. Management names are excluded case-insensitively and adapters cannot replace read/grep/find/ls/bash/edit/write. access must be read-only|mutation|unknown andchildSafe exactlytrue. Description<=4096bytes andredacted. Parameter schema must be object-type,data-only JSON,<=16384bytes,depth<=16,nodes<=2048,no $ref/$dynamicRef. A normalized JSON clone is recursively frozen. Fingerprint SHA covers adapterID,name,origin,access,childSafe,parameters,description,not function code. Owner WeakMap plus reference-aware unregister and optional isAuthorized provides live revocation.

ParentToolInfos marks unregistered tools unknown/ineligible; MCP capability enumeration requires active parent mcp proxy and current adapter. MCP entries need valid server/tool selector,known access and schema; malformed entries are omitted. Generated names use mcp_ plus a sanitized40-character prefix and12hex SHA selector suffix. Dispatch stays with the same current parent adapter. Child selection excludes management,ineligible/unknown and disallowed globs. Omitted tools or exactly['*'] selects eligible non-MCP capabilities. Other glob lists can match MCP names,including mcp_* or mixed['*','read']; contrary to the exact-name comment, selection is not restricted to exact MCP names. Definition mcp selectors separately glob server andtool. Injected delegationTools bypass the ordinary eligibility/disallowed filter; current V2 factory cannot bind agent/control and therefore rejects such a frozen tool set rather than implementing recursion.

At dispatch check preabort,current registration,args nonarrayobject,JSON<=32768bytes andschema. Clone/freeze arguments and context{parentSessionId,runId,cwd,scopeRoots,signal}; cancellation races the promise and postchecks abort,warning that external effects need inspection rather than replay. Adapter remains responsible for remote cleanup. Output recursively redacts secret keys,text andcycles,limits4096nodes/depth8,arrays128/object64/keys128chars,then UTF-8 safe truncates to24576bytes with marker. isError propagates only literal result.isError===true; snapshot details accompany text.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: registerIceDelegableTool,getIceDelegableTools,resolveIceDelegableTool(s),resolveChildTools,createIceDelegableToolDefinitions. API IceDelegableTool includes adapterId,name,origin,access,childSafe:true,description,parameters,execute,isAuthorized?. MCP parent registration is owner-scoped with optional identity; selector dispatch signature(server,tool,params,signal). Existing legacy selected-MCP helper accepts an empty permissive object schema when metadata is absent; active V2 bridge requires schema and uses the general adapter path.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Scoped file tools and guarded V2 child session construction
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
V2 binds exactly the frozen tool names and wraps each in the current permission guard before recording dispatch observations. It loads selected resources deliberately and disables ambient packages/extensions rather than creating a second reasoning loop.

Path admission resolves a prospective path through the nearest existing canonical ancestor,checks approved task roots or read-only resource roots,then canonicalizes again if it exists and rechecks containment. Writer-mode definitions reject any literal .git path component,including read/grep/find/ls built through that family. V2 always uses this writer family,then filters frozen names. Selected skill parent directories expand only read scope; edit/write receive no resource roots. Tool eligibility runs independently after path checks and compares a lowercase requested name to the fixed eligible set. Under subYolo the scoped-path containment check is bypassed,but .git and any existing symlink component remain rejected. Missing ancestors stop the symlink walk. These are path-based checks with ordinary filesystem races,not descriptor-level filesystem isolation.

Bash uses no background registry,exposeSessionEnvironment:false,a whitelist spawn hook and hard maxTimeoutMs(default600000). Thus child Bash cannot adopt background shells and stdin:true fails the ordinary tool prerequisites. Registered adapters are filtered to frozen names; every frozen name must have an actual implementation or the factory throws. The guard runs before observer start; observer marks success on resolved execution when signal is not aborted,even if an adapter result carries isError:true. That distinction affects the afterTool hook success projection and must not be described as semantic tool success. V2 file-evidence observations accept only read/grep/edit/write, so resolved adapter errors do not mint file evidence.

Factory revalidates selected resource hashes; reads/redacts selected contexts and prompts; creates SettingsManager with projectTrusted:false and DefaultResourceLoader disabling packages,extensions,ambient skills,prompt templates,themes. noContextFiles is the inverse of frozen contextFiles,so context files are not categorically disabled. Explicit selected skills are additional paths,contexts append to loader base contexts,and selected prompts append to the system prompt. SDK receives model/modelRuntime,thinking,exactcustomtools,resource/settings/session managers and startup session event. Frozen temperature/topP are not passed by this factory; merely storing them does not establish sampler application. The older wrapSubagentToolDefinitions helper uses a mutable per-run policy box for reused legacy sessions; active V2 uses guard closures and assertChildAuthority instead.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: APIs createScopedReadOnlyToolDefinitions,createScopedWriterToolDefinitions,assertNoSymlinkComponents,assertSubagentToolEligible,buildV2ChildToolDefinitions,createV2ChildSession. V2ChildSessionOptions includes contract,sessionManager,cwd,agentDir,model,modelRuntime?,adapters,guard,observeTool?,bashTimeoutMs?. ChildToolGuard(tool,args,signal) rejects to deny. Session startup event reason=startup. No child plugin auto-loading or recursive management implementation.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Owner-scoped child registry, generation checks, parking and tombstones
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
The registry is the lifecycle owner; UI/RPC only project records. Owner mismatch and deletion appear as unknown IDs. Every accepted/transitioned record is journaled before becoming the in-memory current value.

States starting,running,idle,parked,stopping,blocked,aborted,deleted have the explicit transition table at state-machine41–51; same-state transitions are permitted and increment generation. A completed turn normally returns idle,not terminal. Outcomes completed,failed,cancelled,interrupted,budget_exhausted,timed_out,abandoned,incomplete are separate. accept refuses closed/duplicate,sets starting,generation1,turnInFlight true,zero usage,timestamps,appends anddurablyflushes before storing/emitting. transition checks expected generation and legal edge,patches only result/outcome/usage/blocked metadata,clears blockedReasons away fromblocked,appends,optionallyflushes,then stores/emits. Registry listeners are not isolated from exceptions.

list is owner-filtered andcreation-ordered; inherited records from a fork retain their original owner. resident hides a child while parking. park only idle,marks parking/removes handle before state transition and awaited dispose,finally clears parking. revive shares one promise perID; existing idle resident returns immediately; onlyparked ornonresidentblocked may revive. After async construction it rechecks generation/closed anddisposes stale handles. Blocked revival records reasons without starting a turn; success goes blocked→parked→idle andattaches with failure cleanup. delete requires a legal deleted edge,takes awayresident,writes/flushtombstone first,then disposes/cleans; cleanup failure cannot restore the child.

Patch state open|applying|applied|rejected|unchanged|rollback_conflict is separately journaled with a generation bump anddurableflush; applied/rejected/unchanged are terminal andidempotent only to themselves. restore reconstructs latest records/completions/delivered markers from custom entries without deep schema validation. Resident states becomeparked; in-flight ones gaininterrupted andclear lastResult; aborted/deleted/alreadyparked remain unchanged. Recovery append is not itself explicitly flushed here. disposeAll closes,clears residenthandles andawaits allSettled disposal without rewriting durable state.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: Custom types ice-subagent-v2-child,ice-subagent-v2-completion,ice-subagent-v2-delivered. ChildRecord includes IDs/owner/depth/agent/name?/description,contractHash,transcriptPath,state,generation,turnInFlight,lastTurnOutcome?,lastResult?,blockedReasons?,usage,patch metadata,timestamps. Errors unknown_child|stale_generation|illegal_transition|not_parked|busy. ParentJournal={append,flush,entries}. Residents must expose async dispose.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Durable child completions, parent delivery confirmation and interruption notices
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Completion identity is childID:completed-turn-count and the completion record is durable before delivery. Current runtime waits for transcript confirmation or a finished send before writing the delivered marker; the registry helper's older claim-before-send comment is not the active ordering.

recordCompletion validates owner/child,deduplicates deliveryId,appends/flushtorecordthen emits. claimDelivery writes/flushthe delivered marker once andthen marks memory; it returns undefined forunknown/wrongowner/alreadyclaimed. pendingCompletions filters byowner andunclaimed. Runtime stores outcome,redacted boundedsummary,optionalvalidation summary andtime. Each summary targets16384UTF-8bytes including an output-read continuation marker; the offset subtracts any prepended error anduses retained report bytes. Parent messages label child reports untrusted andsuggest continuation/deletion andsibling state.

flush refuses closed orcompactingparent. While streaming it sends one short steer notice perfreshcompletion using an in-memory noticed set; a rejected steer is swallowed anddoes not remove that noticed mark immediately. Full reports stay pending. Whileidle it selects up to4 pending IDs notalreadyin sending,posts onecustommessage andtracksinflightIDs. message_end confirmation orsuccessful send callsclaimDelivery; rejected send leavespending; finallyclears sending/noticed. triggerTurn defaults true; false recursively posts remainingbatches because no parent turn willlaterflush. Restart restores explicit delivered markers; no scan of preexisting parent completion-message bodies occurs here. Therefore the send/confirm-to-durable-marker crash window is not a transactional exactly-once guarantee,and claims of unconditional at-most-once delivery would be too strong. Confirmed IDs are idempotent.

Idle alerts are separate nondurable custom messages,one perquiet stretch at min(configuredalert,floor(idletimeout/2)); streamingparentgetssteer,idleparentnextTurn. They do not stop the child. Current alert prose says idle-timeout stops it even for silent Bash,although actualBash execution pauses that idle deadline; preserve actual timer behavior in the run entry. Closed-session cancellations become interrupted outcomes with explicit resume advice. Forked children stay with original owners.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: Custom types subagent_completed,subagent_completion_notice,subagent_idle_alert. Completion details {deliveryIds,completions:[{childId,agent,outcome,validation?}],single-child convenience fields?}. APIs flushCompletions({triggerTurn?}),confirmDelivery(message),hasPendingInterruption,inheritedChildren. Completion summary limit16KiB,batch4; output uses agent_control action=output with byte offset. No arbitrary message from a child is trusted as host verification.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Launch preflight, frozen model choice, unique names and staged batch acceptance
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Launch freezes a complete contract for each fresh child, checks the whole batch before acceptance, and retains names for the parent lineage. Provider turns are a separate runTurn action, so accepted does not mean running or completed.

Resolve task.agent, settings.defaultAgent, then the callable catalog; unknown agents report the available list. Delegation permission uses subject agent(name), fallback allow and mode inherit; deny fails preflight, ask is brokered serially before any child acceptance. Task isolation overrides the definition, otherwise none; worktree requires project trust. Resolve current parent tools and adapters, explicit selectors, unavailable-tool diagnostics and the recursion gate. Task.model overrides the definition's ordered model list; resolve the first available configured route or inherited parent through resolveChildModel, retaining skip reasons. The exact lowercase inherit branch uses the captured parent directly. Thinking is task,definition,then medium; parent thinking is not the fallback. Definition source affects rule origin. Scope roots default to cwd, must realpath to existing directories; targets must exist, be regular final non-symlink files, and canonicalize within a root. Ancestor symlinks can canonicalize successfully here; dispatch separately enforces path policy. A non-worktree scope may include external directories, subject to later authority checks.

Preflight pins selected resource hashes, output schema and acceptance, adds fixed child prompt framing plus unavailable-tool diagnostics, generates a child ID and freezes rootSessionId=ownerSessionId with depth0. mcpServers remains an empty array even when tool records select MCP. The task contract is built from task.description with default fields only. SourceHash and resolvedDefinitionHash are equal here. Temperature/topP are stored but their active factory omission is SUB-015.

Names use the validated explicit name or one of100 unused pool names; when exhausted, choose an unused name at the lowest suffix2 or higher. Deleted and fork-inherited names remain reserved. Explicit duplicates within a batch or against prior names fail before acceptance. IDs can be used directly; known inherited IDs/names explain original ownership; missing names list the current names. Catalog cache identity includes cwd, trust, relevant settings and flags, not file mtime; startup/resume/new invalidation is separate.

All delegation approvals and beforeLaunch decision hooks run before persistence. Launch's AbortSignal reaches approval requests but is not forwarded to beforeLaunch hook dispatch. After hooks, recheck owner, parent, settings serialization and child authority. A worktree batch captures one shared dirty parent baseline and rewrites each child's cwd/roots/targets into its separate owned worktree. Stage every durable child transcript, accept every registry record, then construct resident sessions serially. Failure aborts/tombstones accepted children and removes staged worktrees/transcripts, recording cleanup errors where caught. A late factory session after owner shutdown is disposed. These boundaries do not promise a transaction against an OS crash or atomic rollback of all filesystem cleanup.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: V2RuntimeHost supplies getParentSession,getSettings,isProjectTrusted,getParentMode,isSubYolo,getAdapters,optional createChildAgentSession,promptApproval and resource paths. launch(tasks,signal?) returns ChildRecord[]; direct runtime callers have no agent-tool batch schema limit. agent tool limits tasks to1..8. Child names match the contract's1..40-character grammar; IDs ag_ plus26 base32 characters. Fresh launch emits no provider request until runTurn.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Live authority checks, external paths and approval revalidation at dispatch
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
The live guard checks cancellation, budget and authority before executing each tool. Approval grants are temporary child-instance rules and never replace a parent denial.

Before dispatch, reject an aborted signal, ordinary work after the request budget, wrong owner or invalid frozen authority. For read/edit/write, canonicalize prospective paths; edit/write additionally use the protected mutation-path check. Extract all tool subjects and mirror worktree paths into the parent repository for parent policy, while evaluating child rules against the child path. Parent fallback is allow only for active tools, deny otherwise; bridged MCP requires the active parent mcp proxy plus the selected adapter and evaluates both generated-tool and proxy permissions. External-directory subjects take a dedicated early branch: plan denies, build+subYolo allows, otherwise ask; this branch does not apply general ruleSets. A pure read within another owned open patch worktree can omit that external-directory subject, but does not gain mutation permission.

Compose frozen child rules with the parent decision. A resident session grant can turn current child ask into allow only when parent allows and the shell subject is not opaque. Parent deny is final. Ask requests contain child identity, tool, bounded/redacted summary, foreground flag and an optional offered rule. Summaries replace whitespace runs with a visible newline marker and cap the subject preview at300 characters. A simple Bash subject offers its command-prefix rule; opaque Bash offers no session grant. Non-Bash can offer the tool rule. The request identity combines childID,time and randomness.

After broker allow, recheck abort, budget, owner/frozen authority and current parent decision before storing an offered session rule or invoking the tool. Permission succeeds before the beforeTool decision hook. Current-authority validation compares owner, frozen tool identity/access/fingerprint, available model, subYolo, parent mode, trust for project resources/worktrees, parent policy hash and every selected resource's canonical identity/content hash. It can block on policy changes even if an individual invocation would otherwise be allowed. The launch-enabled setting is checked at fresh launch; current-authority validation does not globally revoke an existing child merely because enabled becomes false.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: ChildToolGuard(tool,args,signal) is the dispatch boundary. ApprovalAnswer=allow-once|allow-session|deny; grants remain resident-memory state. Parent policy derives from current active tool names, settings ruleSets, mode and adapter identity; frozen child policy remains in ChildRuntimeContract. Guard errors become ordinary tool execution failures in the child loop.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Admission, liveness deadlines and abandonment of uncooperative child turns
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
A parent owner has a configurable admission pool. Accepted turn intent is durable before admission, while timers start only after a permit is acquired. An uncooperative aborted turn is fenced from later result publication.

runTurn rejects unknown, nonresident, already-running or patch-closed children despite its older 'never throws' comment. It validates narrowed acceptance and authority, cancels retirement, publishes turnInFlight=true durably, then invokes accepted(). This acknowledgement can precede a concurrency slot. acquire loops until a permit is available; waiting promises are queued and a release wakes one. A wake is not a reserved permit, so a newcomer can win the next acquisition; do not claim strict FIFO admission. Caller abort removes a queued waiter. No queue timeout runs before admission, and the pool/maxConcurrent is captured when the owner is constructed rather than rebuilt on every settings change.

After admission, start wall and idle deadlines, default1800000ms and600000ms, plus an idle alert at min(configured alert, floor(idleTimeout/2)); configured0 disables the alert. Model/tool activity rearms idle and alert timers. Only in-flight Bash increments the counter that pauses the idle deadline; a silent long non-Bash tool can still reach it. Bash still has its tool ceiling and the child wall deadline, and still receives idle alerts. Track startedAt,lastActivityAt,current tool/arguments for status; send at most one alert per quiet stretch. The alert is informational, delivered as steer when the parent is busy and nextTurn when idle.

Caller cancellation is attached after the internal abort-grace listener, then pre-aborted signals are applied. Expiry records the deadline reason and aborts. After10000ms without settlement, mark finishClaimed/fenced, clear timers, release the admission permit once, clear foreground and record abandoned with explicit unknown last-tool effects. The underlying promise may still be running; resident.running remains until its real settlement, and late settlement cannot record a second outcome. This releases TypeScript concurrency before every underlying effect is known to stop. Native cleanup-permit retention is a stronger resource bound worth preserving.

On admitted start, recheck authority, persist running, install the bounded-turn wrapper and emit started observation. Queued cancellation reports cancelled and may delete a never-run child without a patch. Provider stop, error, length and empty-text outcomes are classified separately; cancellation or deadline overrides completion. Finalization claims the outcome before asynchronous acceptance hooks, preventing grace from double-publishing while bookkeeping completes. Timers/listeners/budget state and permits are cleaned up. Finish records usage and validated output durably, and closes unchanged worktrees. Idle children retire after30000ms if not displayed, foreground, running or in a patch operation; excess idle residents are parked oldest-first beyond8, and that separate excess-parking path does not consult displayed status.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: States live separately from ChildTurnOutcome completed|failed|cancelled|timed_out|budget_exhausted|incomplete|abandoned|interrupted. runTurn options foreground,background,acceptance,accepted,signal. Overview capacity={running,queued,max}; queued means a turn promise exists but admitted=false. Liveness status includes elapsed/quiet age and last tool or waiting-on-model. Retirement is a memory policy, not a deletion of persistent identity.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Model-request budgets, one tool-free wrap-up and temporary retry suppression
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
ChildTurnBudget wraps the existing session stream/stop/tool hooks rather than adding a second loop. Active V2 gives each run100 model requests, then at most one tool-free wrap-up.

Count a model request before calling the stream function; authorize current child state and abort status first. This counts wrapper stream invocations, not necessarily internal HTTP retries inside a provider. Record completed assistant usage once per message using a WeakSet; the generic tracker counts input+cacheWrite+output tokens, excluding cacheRead, and checks turns before tokens before elapsed time. Active V2 passes maxTurns=100; generic token/time budget helpers are retained APIs, not public V2 settings. Reaching the last request with a normal stop can remain completed; cutting off a request that still needs tools marks budget_exhausted. Ordinary tools assert the budget before effects.

During the bounded run, disable automatic session retry and compaction and save prior settings/hooks/stream state. Restore them on disposal. A budget interruption permits a single wrap-up: clear queued messages, remove active tools, cap output to1024 tokens, set a30000ms abort timer, and ask for a report using only existing context. Restore the active tool list afterward, clear the queue again, and clear the timer when complete; queued contents are discarded, not restored. The timeout calls session.abort; a noncooperative prompt can still outlive that local await, with outer turn cancellation/abandonment providing the broader terminal path. Never describe the wrap-up as proof that every tool or provider stopped.

The generic resolveTurnBudget helper accepts only positive integer limits and can narrow, never raise or remove, an existing ceiling. claimWrapUp is one-shot. Active runtime observes assistant and compaction usage separately for billing, while disabling automatic compaction during these runs. Final outcome classification does not turn a wrap-up report into independently verified success.

The current wrapper sets only maxTokens at turn-budget.ts:95 and :109, not hardMaxOutputTokens. The 1024 value is therefore the ordinary allowance presented to the provider adapter, not proof of an immutable final wire limit: reasoning-budget adjustment or a payload callback can widen an ordinary maxTokens value. Suppression at lines130-144 changes session retry/compaction enabled flags; it does not set provider maxRetries and therefore does not disable or restore internal HTTP retries. AI-006 documents the distinct hard-limit contract that a strengthened port should use.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: Constants MAX_CHILD_MODEL_REQUESTS_PER_RUN=100; CHILD_WRAP_UP_LIMITS maxTokens=1024,timeoutMs=30000. ChildTurnBudget interrupted(),assertOrdinaryWork(),wrapUp(signal),dispose(). Generic TurnBudget maxTurns?,maxTokens?,timeoutMs?; counters remain per-run. No automatic retry-safe fallback execution is wired through retained legacy routing helpers.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Resume, steering, stop and deletion of persistent child instances
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Revival reopens the child's durable transcript and frozen contract, checks ownership/hash/current authority and worktree existence/ownership, resolves the frozen model, and only then attaches a resident session. Blocked reasons remain visible without manufacturing a live handle.

continueChild refuses a closed patch or patch operation, revives parked/blocked children and runs a new turn. It may add task-local acceptance to the frozen baseline but cannot replace model, scope, tools, isolation or output schema. Resume-added criteria do not mutate the persistent baseline: a later turn without those additions requires only the original criteria. Interrupted revival adds a recovery notice listing unmatched tool calls and their unknown effects; it does not replay them. One child cannot run two turns concurrently.

send(message) while running uses session.steer; send(followup) queues session.followUp. For an idle child, message revives if needed and appends a pending note without starting provider work; followup starts a new background turn. interrupt aborts, awaits resident.running, then starts the follow-up. That await is unbounded for an uncooperative underlying promise, unlike stop. stop aborts and waits at most10500ms for a running turn; the run's10000ms grace can report abandoned. detachToBackground only changes resident foreground/background bookkeeping; it does not itself detach a caller AbortSignal already installed by runTurn.

Delete refuses applying/rollback_conflict or another patch operation, stops the child, writes the registry tombstone before disposal/cleanup, removes an owned worktree and releases output artifacts. Disposal can still await session.abort, so delete is not globally bounded merely because stop is. Shutdown closes the owner, cancels broker requests/timers and all resident controllers, waits for running turns up to10500ms and disposeAll up to10000ms, then clears owner state. Stale factory/revival handles are disposed rather than reattached. Closing-session cancellation becomes interrupted for restart delivery.

outputOf returns a clone of the saved latest result. Interrupted state without a valid saved result returns undefined instead of recycling a previous verified answer. Legacy transcript fallback takes the latest nonempty assistant text, redacts and caps it at48KiB, and labels it unverified_plain with cumulative usage. A result snapshot can remain available after an unchanged worktree has been cleaned, even though its previously checked evidence paths no longer exist.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: continueChild(id,prompt,{foreground,acceptance?,signal?,accepted?}); send(id,text,kind=followup), kind=message|followup|interrupt; stop(id); delete(id); shutdown(); detachToBackground(ids); outputOf(id). IDs and reserved names resolve within the owner lineage. Patch decisions are independent of turn outcome and can permanently close continuation.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Agent tool batches, background acknowledgement and foreground detachment
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
The tool validates the strict task schema and resume exclusions, normalizes every context packet, resolves references, launches fresh children, then dispatches fresh and resumed turns in original task order. Background acknowledgement means durable turn acceptance, not a completed result or guaranteed admission.

agent requires1..8 tasks; each requires description1..120 characters and prompt with maxLength65536. Optional fields include agent,name,resume,model,thinking,isolation,scope,outputSchema,acceptance and context. On resume, reject outputSchema,agent,name,model,thinking,isolation and scope before launching fresh siblings. Context/acceptance remain permitted. All context packets are normalized before effects. Existing name/ID references are resolved before fresh launch, but full resumed contract/runtime availability is checked only when continueChild runs afterward. A mixed fresh/resume batch can therefore persist fresh children before a resumed child fails authority, busy or patch checks; do not advertise all-or-nothing behavior across those cases.

With background=true, create one acceptance promise per run; runTurn's accepted callback follows durable turn intent and may precede admission. Return accepted IDs and immediate rejections after those acknowledgements, while child result promises continue with handlers. Caller signal is forwarded to launch approvals, but not to background runTurn. Rejected background resumes are reported as rejected failed results and are never counted as started. A later background failure travels through the completion mechanism, not a claimed aggregate result.

Foreground dispatch passes caller cancellation, waits concurrently, and maintains an abort listener that stops accepted children. A250ms poll releases the wait when hasPendingSteering becomes true; queued follow-up alone does not release it. Ctrl+B releases registered blocking waits. foregroundDetachMs defaults60000,0 disables the timer. Either release path marks still-running children background, returns ordered IDs with detached=true and explains how to inspect them; already completed results remain accessible. Removing the tool-level abort listener does not remove the runTurn signal listener itself. A500ms progress timer emits only changed summaries. All listeners/timers/wait registration are cleaned up.

When every foreground turn settles, format per-child reports in input order and, for a multi-child batch, prepend deterministic host batch synthesis. Result details omit large text but retain IDs,outcomes,usage,validation and synthesis. Model-visible text is redacted then head-truncated at2000 lines and65536-256 bytes with a presentation marker. Error catches return normal text results without setting isError, so consumers must inspect the stated outcome/details instead of assuming a transport error flag.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: Tool agent({tasks:AgentTaskInput[],background?:boolean}). Scope roots1..32 and targets<=32 strings; acceptance<=16 strings maxLength1024; context has<=16 typed items. Foreground returns structured result details; background details {ids,rejected}; detached details include ordered ids and detached=true. No legacy delegate/review_batch tool is registered by V2.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Agent control queries, range output and repeated-wait suppression
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
agent_control resolves ids in preference to id and checks supplied references even for actions that later use the whole list. Queries project registry/runtime state; lifecycle operations call the same owner methods as the UI.

Actions are list,status,wait,output,send,resume,stop,delete,agents. ids permits1..8 references. list reports children and descriptions; status includes current state, turn count, model/patch information and liveness. Tokens in status include input,output,cacheRead,cacheWrite, whereas overview live token totals use input+output. agents lists the definition catalog. send requires a message and acts on the first selected child, defaulting to followup; resume,stop and delete process selected IDs serially.

wait uses registry subscriptions and a predicate requiring turnInFlight=false and state neither running nor starting; an idle-looking queued continuation is not settled. Default timeout60000ms, schema range1..1800000. The signature includes selected IDs,state,generation,turnInFlight. If the same signature timed out less than30000ms ago, return immediately with the unchanged-wait explanation rather than block again. A state change or elapsed cooldown allows another wait. Ctrl+B and a250ms hasPendingSteering poll end only the parent wait; they do not stop children. External abort also ends the wait, but this wrapper installs its abort listener without first checking an already-aborted signal, unlike runTurn. It can classify an unlabelled abort as timedOut and update the repeated-wait record. Do not claim universal pre-abort immediacy for this tool.

output without offset/length formats each selected child's saved result with assurance. A range request requires exactly one child and delegates to runtime.readOutput. The public schema caps offset at4194304 and length at49152; the internal store accepts reads to65536. Output reports totalBytes,bytesRead,nextOffset,eof,sha256,truncated and content type. Inline and artifact ranges share UTF-8 boundary checks, so callers can append chunks without corruption. Deleted/cross-owner/unknown children fail owner lookup. All control text uses the common64KiB/2000-line presentation cap; caught errors are normal text, not isError=true.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: agent_control action vocabulary above; id?,ids?,message?,delivery=message|followup|interrupt,timeoutMs?,offset?,length?. Registry wait returns {timedOut,records}. Host control bridge separately exposes stop|resume|delete|send. Range output retains artifactId only for artifact-backed data, not a model-supplied filesystem path.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Selected child resources and explicit untrusted context packets
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Resource resolution records source and canonical path plus content hash during preflight, and revalidates those fields before session creation/revival and current-authority dispatch. Parent-supplied context is separately framed as untrusted data.

User roots are agentDir/skills,prompts,context; project roots are the nearest .ice/skills and .ice/prompts, with project context rooted at cwd. Named resources try user first and project second. Skills select name/SKILL.md, prompts name.md, context the given name. Explicit absolute, ./, slash or backslash paths resolve from cwd and must be lexically inside an allowed root. Candidate names must be nonempty and no more than4096 code units/UTF-8 bytes. Each kind permits16 selections, canonical duplicates are removed within that kind, each file is<=128KiB, and aggregate selected bytes are<=512KiB. Stat and bounded read enforce individual size. Project content requires trust. Selected skill parent directories extend read-only resource roots.

Resolution canonicalizes both root and candidate and requires containment. In the explicit-path loop, an existing explicit project file can be examined against an existing user root first and throw as outside that root before trying project; this is a reachable source quirk, not a claim that explicit project paths always work. Revalidation checks aggregate metadata, canonical source identity and exact bounded content SHA; changed resources reject rather than silently reload. Selected prompts remove frontmatter and trim/redact their body. Selected contexts are redacted into child resources; trust never comes from file prose.

normalizeSubagentContextPacket accepts a packet with items plus optional legacyContext. legacyContext becomes a parent-context item after trim/redaction. Combined item count<=16; IDs trim and match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}, kinds are parent_note|verified_fact|evidence_ref|artifact_ref, and content is nonempty after trim/redaction. Duplicate IDs reject rather than deduplicate. Per-item content<=32768UTF-8 bytes and total<=262144. Freeze packet/items and append their id,kind,content under explicit untrusted framing to the task prompt. There is no ambient parent conversation fork in active V2 launch merely because the older prompt-cache helper exists.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: resolveSubagentResources({skills?,prompts?,context?},{cwd,agentDir,projectTrusted}); revalidateSubagentResources; loadSelectedPromptContent; normalizeSubagentContextPacket; withContextPacket. Stored resource fields kind,name,source,sourcePath,canonicalPath,sourceHash. Task context schema supplies typed items; direct legacyContext helper remains a retained API.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Bounded report envelope and local output-schema validation
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
V2 selects structured_report when the task has outputSchema, any acceptance criteria, or agent name exactly review; otherwise plain_final_turn stays explicitly unverified. Shape parsing precedes observed-evidence acceptance.

The local schema subset permits only type,properties,required,items,additionalProperties. Reject unknown keys, refs, unions and remote schemas. Serialized schema<=8192bytes, maximum depth5,nodes64,object properties16,required16,property-name64bytes matching the declared letter/alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen pattern. Root must be object and every object requires additionalProperties=false; absent properties/required become empty, required names must exist and are deduplicated. Arrays require items. Primitive types string,number,integer,boolean,null are supported; irrelevant but otherwise allowed schema keys on a primitive are silently dropped rather than rejected. Values enforce finite number,safe integer,strings<=8192bytes,arrays<=64items and payload JSON<=16384bytes; object extras reject. The returned normalized payload is cloned and top-level frozen, not recursively frozen by this parser.

The final report is bounded at24KiB before parsing. Empty/oversize input gets malformed/truncated status. Parse direct JSON, otherwise try balanced objects beginning at at most8 opening braces with quoted-string/escape handling. The first parseable object is accepted for shape checking; a wrong-shaped first object does not cause a search for a later valid report. Require nonempty trimmed summary and evidence.paths with1..64 nonempty paths<=4096bytes. Extra envelope/evidence keys are not rejected. Summary is bounded by total report size rather than a separate small field limit. Requested payload is mandatory and schema-checked; unrequested payload is ignored.

Optional findings permit<=32 entries with severity low|medium|high,category nonempty<=256bytes,claim nonempty<=8192bytes and1..16 evidence paths. Optional requirements permit<=16 claims,nonempty id<=64bytes and one of satisfied|partial|failed|not_run|not_applicable; note is retained only when a string<=1024bytes; evidencePaths<=64 can be empty at parse time. Duplicate requirement IDs are first-claim-wins. Parser path discovery for malformed output is diagnostic only and never verifies evidence. Structured provider output truncated by a length stop is not accepted, even if its prefix is valid JSON. No repair-model request or verification command is launched here.
certified_entry_comparisons.interfaces: normalizeSubagentOutputSchema,validateSubagentPayload,parseSubagentReport,normalizePlainFinalAnswer. Report shape {summary,evidence:{paths},payload?,findings?,requirements?}. Parse and final-validation outcomes are separate; raw final text remains retained on validation failure. V2ResultValidation assurance is decided by SUB-027, not envelope fields such as testsPassed.

certified_entry_comparisons.title: Per-turn observed file evidence, acceptance criteria and honest assurance
certified_entry_comparisons.mechanism:
Each run creates a fresh V2ResultObservations object. Previous turns, siblings, model prose and directory listings cannot satisfy the current turn's evidence requirements.

Observe only read,grep,edit,write with string args.path. At dispatch after approval, resolve the prospective canonical path and require an approved root. read/grep need a preexisting regular file; grep over a directory does not create evidence for every match. Capture at most1024 distinct paths. After successful execution and no abort, require the same canonical identity and a regular final non-symlink file. For read/grep, dev/ino,size,mtime,ctime must be unchanged before/after; for edit/write, record the post-operation stat. Final citations resolve first against child cwd, then roots, must canonicalize within scope, and must still match the recorded stat. These metadata checks are evidence-of-access/stability, not cryptographic content or semantic proof. Bash,ls,find and custom adapters do not add V2 file evidence.

Normalize frozen acceptance plus task-local additions: each input list<=16, each raw string<=1024UTF-8 bytes and nonempty after trim; redact/trim,deduplicate and require<=16 unique criteria. IDs criterion-1 etc follow normalized position. A claim verifies only when status=satisfied, evidencePaths is nonempty and every path passes the current observation check. Every required baseline/additional criterion must verify. All top-level report paths and finding evidence also must pass. A valid structured report with zero criteria can be verified when its other evidence checks pass. Payload is exposed only on a verified result.

Plain final turns always return verified=false and assurance=unverified_plain even on outcome completed. Noncompleted turns are not promoted. Structured completed work that fails validation becomes failed with raw answer and diagnostics retained. Successful V2 structured validation returns evidence_checked, with semanticVerified=false,commandsObserved=false,commandsPassed=false,reviewerVerified=false. Calling the agent review or writing testsPassed:true does not change that level.
